models.purpose: Judge whether the existing stations can serve a fully electric fleet.
models.summary: Vehicles in a region equal density times area times ownership per capita times electric share. Arrivals are Poisson and each supercharger is an M/M/1 desk, so the mean queue is lambda squared over mu times mu minus lambda. A convenience index compares vehicles needing a charge with what the stations can serve; below 1 the area is convenient. Ownership per capita is 0.94 urban, 0.83 suburban, 0.60 rural, and a station covers 170 miles.

variables.definition: cars owned per person in the region

governing_equations.purpose: mean queue length at one supercharger

objectives: Judge whether the existing stations can serve a fully electric fleet.
constraints: a station is convenient only when the index is below 1

parameter_estimation.method: ownership taken from a cited US statistic, utilization 35 percent from General Motors

assumptions: a built station is never removed

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: the convenience map covers most of the US but mu is not numbered

validation_refs: connectivity rate of 71 percent against the Tesla map
strengths: each region is solved separately and then summed
limitations: the service rate mu is used but never given a value
missing_details: the service rate mu of the M/M/1 station is not given a number

models.purpose: Split charging stations across three regions at minimum cost and minimum wait.
models.summary: Two objectives: building cost of destination and supercharging stations, and a weighted average of their waiting times. Distance, convenience and vehicle constraints close the model. Solved in MATLAB with 8.8 chargers per station, the result is 1,704,500 stations: 1,142,015 urban, 392,035 suburban, 170,450 rural. The summary rounds this to about 1.7 million and a 67 to 23 to 10 split. The sensitivity table reprints the total as 1,704,500 and also as 1704500.

governing_equations.source_expression: min Z = r_DC * C_DC + r_SC * C_SC
governing_equations.purpose: building cost of both station types

objectives: Split charging stations across three regions at minimum cost and minimum wait.
constraints: superchargers tied to destination stations by an efficiency ratio

parameter_estimation.method: 8.8 chargers per station from the cited statistics

assumptions: station prices differ by type and are treated as constants

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: one solution per region, summed to 1,704,500

validation_refs: connectivity rate of 71 percent against the Tesla map
strengths: each region is solved separately and then summed
limitations: the summary says about 1.7 million while the body prints 1,704,500 and 15 million chargers
missing_details: the service rate mu of the M/M/1 station is not given a number

models.purpose: Predict the electric share from the indexes that survive a significance test.
models.summary: Six indexes are defined. A logistic regression in SAS keeps three: wealth distribution, policy orientation and government investment. For the whole country the log odds equal 0.1110 plus 1.7137 times wealth plus 1.5000 times policy plus 1.614 times investment. The fitted timeline puts a 10 percent share in 2024 and 90 to 100 percent in 2069. A lag index is introduced to compare charger construction with sales, but its definition is not consistent across the section.

variables.definition: policy orientation, proxied by the subsidy
predicted market share of electric vehicles

governing_equations.purpose: log odds of the electric share for the whole country

objectives: Predict the electric share from the indexes that survive a significance test.

parameter_estimation.method: maximum likelihood, indexes dropped when they fail the SAS test

assumptions: the six indexes capture the drivers of adoption

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: three of six indexes survive; the timeline is tabulated but not back-tested

validation_refs: connectivity rate of 71 percent against the Tesla map
strengths: each region is solved separately and then summed
limitations: the lag index is defined three ways in one section and the three do not agree
missing_details: the service rate mu of the M/M/1 station is not given a number
